tasks.short: Redeem coupons or stamps and issue a stamp card at the till.

steps.what: Hand over coupons or trading stamps
Scan coupons or stamps on the point-of-sale
Apply coupon rules to the open basket
Tell the customer the balance or refusal
Decide a disputed coupon or stamp override

tasks.design: The promotion table already in the {OTHER} point-of-sale applies a coupon, meal voucher or stamp when the code, date and basket match. The cashier still scans the item and explains a refusal. A duty supervisor approves an override only against that refusal version. Native till rules are used before any custom code.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper trading stamps and local voucher schemes had no code the till could read, so the cashier keyed each value from a leaflet.
tasks.enabler_now: Most meal vouchers and store coupons now carry a barcode, and the till already has a promotion table with dates, values and product lists.
tasks.still_hard: Paper stamps, damaged codes, and schemes that change the rule without sending a file. A forged paper voucher still needs a person.
tasks.human_edge: The cashier sees a taped-over barcode or an altered date, and explains a refusal without turning the queue hostile.
tasks.altitude: The cashier still stands at the till. Keying of standard vouchers drops; explaining a refusal stays. The right to override a refusal stays with the duty supervisor.

reach.task: Apply a coded discount to a rental charge
reach.learn: Put the discount in the same rule table and keep a supervisor on the exception only.

evidence.claim: A till promotion table can price a voucher when code, date and basket match, so the cashier stops keying the value.
Tools fit to monitor staff, including per-cashier variance reports, need works-council consent.

assumptions: The cashier's boundary is the tender moment. Scheme contracts and the ledger posting sit outside this task.

Voucher fields are code, scheme id, expiry date, value in cents, eligible item list and a one-per-basket flag. The scheme file or the printed barcode produces them. If the code will not scan, the cashier keys those fields and the duty supervisor approves.
The shop tests the till's own promotion settings before anyone writes a custom check.
An override log that names the cashier is treated like a per-cashier variance report for works-council consent. The design does not rank cashiers.
Food stamps in this European shop means meal vouchers and similar social vouchers, not a US benefit card.
unknowns: Which voucher schemes this shop still accepts, and whether paper trading stamps still exist.
Who is allowed to change the promotion table, and whether the works council has already consented to till logs that name the cashier.
research_questions: What share of voucher tenders still has no barcode?
Does the current point-of-sale already reject an expired or wrong-item code without a manual key?

already_counted.description: Scanning a coded voucher and explaining the till's refusal
Duty supervisor deciding a disputed override

incremental.description: Cashier flags vouchers the rule table rejects in error
Promo owner loads coupon and meal-voucher rules into the till

approvals.approved_version: override request v1 with voucher code, basket id and refusal reason

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central case prices coded meal vouchers and coupons from the till table and assumes paper trading stamps are gone. If a third of tenders are still paper stamps, the cashier keeps keying those and saving falls toward the low end. The three hours for flagging bad rules are already taken off the central figure. A scheme file that arrives late each week is the low case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Post a guest or patient charge onto the open account.

steps.what: Send coded charges for a guest or patient
Match charges to the guest folio or patient account
Resolve a missing or doubled account id
Post coded charges on the folio at tariff
Review uncoded or high-value patient charges
Post the reviewed charges to the folio account

tasks.design: The outlet till posts a coded charge to the {OTHER} guest folio or patient account when account id, item code and amount match the tariff. The cashier only resolves a missing or doubled id, and reviews an uncoded or high-value line before that reviewed version posts. The account system's own posting is tried before a custom link. The charge line carries no clinical note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Outlet slips were paper or free text, so the cashier retyped every amount onto the account and matched names by eye.
tasks.enabler_now: Outlet tills already store item codes, and folio systems already accept a charge when the account id is known. The gap is the retype, not the arithmetic.
tasks.still_hard: Two guests with the same name, a ward slip with no id, and a tariff that does not list the item. A patient account may be health data even when the line is only a code and an amount.
tasks.human_edge: The cashier knows which of two open accounts is the person at the desk, and spots a charge that cannot belong to that stay.

ambition.what: Refuse an uncoded guest or patient charge while the account is still open, instead of finding it at checkout.

tasks.altitude: The cashier stops retyping routine slips. The week shifts to the exception queue and disputes at the desk. They can hold an uncoded charge; they do not gain the right to change the tariff.

reach.task: Post a damage fee onto a rental account
reach.learn: Post a coded tariff line straight through, and hold an uncoded fee for a person to review.

evidence.claim: Guest-folio and patient-account systems can post a coded charge from an outlet when the account id is already known.
A decision based solely on automated processing that has a significant effect on a person is barred.
A patient account can carry health data, so the posted line should keep item code and amount and leave clinical notes out.

assumptions: The cashier's boundary is the open guest or patient account. The general ledger and the insurer's claim sit outside this task.

Charge fields are account id, item code, quantity, amount in cents, outlet id and timestamp. The outlet till produces them. If the id is missing, the cashier types those fields from the slip. No diagnosis text is a field.
The team tests the folio system's own charge import before building a separate integration.
A standard tariff post is a configured price, not a decision about the person. Uncoded and high-value lines stay with the cashier because a wrong charge changes what that person pays.
Outlet staff keep confirming the item on their own screen; only the paper slip is removed. That residual time is already counted and is not the cashier's saving.
unknowns: Whether these accounts are hotel folios, clinic invoices, or both.
The amount above which a charge counts as high-value, and who owns the tariff table.
Whether national health-privacy rules treat the account id as special-category data in this setting.
research_questions: What share of charge slips arrive with a stable account id and an item code?
Does the folio system already import an outlet charge, and where does that import fail?

already_counted.description: Resolving a bad account id and reviewing uncoded or high-value charges
Outlet staff still confirm the item they recorded

incremental.description: Cashier clears a wrong tariff match and fixes the map entry that caused it
Billing lead maintains the outlet tariff table

approvals.approved_version: charge review v1 with account id, item code, amount and tariff result

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central case posts coded outlet charges without retyping and leaves the cashier on bad ids and uncoded lines. If half of slips arrive as free text, the match stays manual and saving falls toward the low end. Patient accounts with no stable id are in that low case. The five hours of tariff-map fixes are already taken off the central figure.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compute each sale total and record the session totals.

steps.what: Add the basket and show the amount due
Tell the customer the total and take tender
Store the paid sale on the till session
Read session totals by payment type
Copy session totals onto the cash-up sheet

tasks.design: The {OTHER} point-of-sale already adds the basket and stores each paid sale. At closing the cashier reads session totals by payment type on that till, and that same snapshot goes to {ERP}. The copy onto a paper cash-up sheet stops. The cashier still tells the customer the amount due and takes the tender.
tasks.previous_blocker: The till total and the ledger sat in different places, so someone copied the session figures onto a sheet for finance.
tasks.enabler_now: The till already shows expected totals by payment type at closing. Sending that snapshot to the ledger is configuration and a file handoff, not a new calculator.
tasks.still_hard: A till with no session export still needs the sheet. A total the customer disputes is a conversation, not a posting problem.
tasks.human_edge: The cashier notices a doubled scan or a missing tender before the customer leaves, which the session total cannot see.
tasks.altitude: The week at the till does not change. The end-of-shift copy disappears. The cashier gains no new decision right; finance reads the till snapshot instead of the sheet.

reach.learn: Send the session total from the till to the ledger and stop keeping a second sheet.

evidence.claim: A named till shows expected totals per payment type at closing, and staff enter the count.
The amount due on a sale is already computed by the point-of-sale when the basket is rung.

assumptions: The cashier's boundary is the sale and the session snapshot. Counting the drawer is a separate task. Posting the ledger journal is finance work.

Session-total fields are session id, till id, payment type, amount in cents and close timestamp. The point-of-sale produces them. If the export fails, the cashier reads the closing screen and finance keys those fields once.
No per-cashier ranking is built. If a later report names the cashier, works-council consent is a new question and is not part of this saving.
The one hour for re-sending a missed export is extra upkeep, not part of the closing screen the cashier already reads.
unknowns: Whether this till can already export a session snapshot, and which payment types it splits.
Who in finance currently rekeys the cash-up sheet, so that work is not dropped on the floor.
research_questions: How many minutes a cashier spends copying the closing totals, separate from counting cash?
Does the ledger already accept a till session file?

already_counted.description: Telling the customer the total and reading the closing screen

incremental.description: Cashier re-sends a session export that did not arrive

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central case removes only the cash-up copy. The customer conversation and the till's own arithmetic stay, and they are most of the hour. If this till cannot send session totals to the ledger, the copy stays and saving sits at the low end. The hour for a failed export is already taken off the central figure.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Sort, count and wrap notes and coins from the drawer.

steps.what: Show the till expected cash for the drawer
Sort notes and coins by denomination
Count currency from the sorted drawer
Wrap coins and strap notes into bundles
Enter the count beside the till cash figure
Witness the count against the till figure

tasks.design: The cashier still sorts, counts and wraps the drawer by hand. The {OTHER} point-of-sale shows the expected cash for that drawer, the cashier enters the denomination count beside it, and the screen shows the difference. A duty supervisor witnesses that deposit-count version before the bundles go to the safe. No per-cashier league table is added.
tasks.previous_blocker: The expected cash lived on a closing slip and the count lived on a deposit slip, so the cashier subtracted the two by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: A current till already shows expected totals by payment type at closing, and staff already enter the count. The subtraction is the only part to drop.
tasks.still_hard: Notes and coins still have to be handled. A till that cannot show expected cash leaves the subtraction in place. A shortage still needs a person, not a rule.
tasks.human_edge: The cashier feels a short bundle, spots a counterfeit note, and recounts a denomination the screen cannot see.
tasks.altitude: The week still ends with a drawer on the desk. The hand subtraction goes. The cashier does not decide the shortage alone; the duty supervisor still witnesses the count.

reach.role: gambling change person and booth cashier
reach.task: Count a booth drawer of notes and coins
reach.learn: Enter the count beside the booth system's expected cash and keep the wrap in the person's hands.

evidence.claim: A named till shows expected totals per payment type at closing, and staff enter the count.
Sorting, counting and wrapping notes and coins is physical work and stays with the person at the drawer.
Tools fit to monitor staff, including per-cashier variance reports, need works-council consent.

assumptions: The cashier's boundary is this drawer's count and wrap. The bank deposit run and the ledger posting sit outside the task.

Deposit-count fields are denomination, pieces, amount in cents, till expected cash in cents and session id. The cashier enters pieces; the till produces the expected cash. If the till figure is missing, the cashier writes both numbers on the deposit slip and the supervisor still witnesses them.
The design uses the closing screen the till already has. It does not add a report that ranks cashiers. A recount after a difference is the half hour of extra upkeep below.

Dual control already exists where the shop requires a witness. This task does not invent a second count for shops that do not do one; the six percent is the witness where that control is already the practice, and shops without it keep that share as unused.
unknowns: Whether this till already shows expected cash, or only a grand total.
Whether a second person already witnesses the count in this shop.
research_questions: How often the hand subtraction is the step that hides a shortage?
Does the works council already treat the closing screen as a monitoring tool?

already_counted.description: Sorting, counting, wrapping and entering the denomination count
Duty supervisor witnessing the deposit count

incremental.description: Recounts when the entered count and the till figure disagree

approvals.approved_version: deposit count v1 by denomination with till expected cash

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central case removes only the hand subtraction of the count from the till's expected cash. Sorting, counting and wrapping stay. If the till does not show expected cash, nothing is saved and the result sits at the low end. The half hour of recounts is already taken off the central figure.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still at the till and the drawer. Copying session totals, retyping guest charges and keying standard vouchers shrink. The cashier can hold an uncoded charge before checkout. A voucher override and the cash witness stay with the duty supervisor. Counting notes and coins does not move.
reach: Counter and rental clerks: send the session total to the ledger instead of a second sheet, and post a coded damage fee the same way as a folio charge.
Gambling change persons and booth cashiers: enter a drawer count beside the booth's expected cash and keep the wrap in the person's hands.
skills_to_grow: Explaining a voucher refusal from the till's reason
Resolving a duplicated guest or patient account without a clinical note
Entering a denomination count once beside the till figure
role.ambitious_version: The till holds voucher rules, guest tariffs and session totals, so a standard tender or a coded charge posts itself. The cashier's attention stays on a refused voucher, a nameless guest and the physical cash. Guest charges show on the account the same day. The drawer is still counted and wrapped by hand, with a witness on the figure the person entered.
